events.summary: Funds were sent to district secretariats for May elderly allowance payments.
Health authorities reauthorised conditional Triposha use for young children.
An MP allocated funds for development work at a Vavuniya temple.
Minister instructed officials to halt military land acquisition surveys in Jaffna.
Mahaweli Authority opened five Polgolla Reservoir spill gates after heavy rain.
Cabinet paper proposed restarting three halted middle-income housing projects.
Cabinet approved social protection relief for workers aged 55 and above.
Authorities planned special bus services for Poson full-moon holiday travel.
President allocated funding for Sunnakam college auditorium construction.
First tranche released for Sunnakam college auditorium construction.
Authorities decided to remove dangerous trees across Colombo municipal area.
Cabinet approved appointing an expert committee on public-service salary disparities.
Cabinet approved seeking private-sector support for wildlife lodge infrastructure upgrades.
Court temporarily halted Eastern Province graduate teacher appointments.
ICT scholarship application deadline extended to 7 June for eligible students.
President distributed 5,400 Urumaya land deeds to Vavuniya and Mannar residents.
Eastern Province governor provided machinery for waste removal and agricultural development.
Government plans to issue 1,376 additional free Urumaya deeds in Mullaitivu.
Dangerous rocks will be removed from the Colombo-Kandy Road at Kadugannawa.
Minister ordered immediate reconstruction works in weather-affected plantation areas.
President opened a Netherlands-supported rehabilitation and mental-health centre.
President instructed officials to investigate and resolve Kappapulavu land issues.
Government announced a dengue eradication week in high-risk areas.
President distributed 1,286 free land deeds in Kilinochchi.
President opened Kilinochchi women’s healthcare centre.
President distributed 1,286 Urumaya land deeds in Jaffna.
Government announced restarting the halted Northern Province housing programme next year.
Government approved 250 staff appointments to accelerate land deed processing.
Cabinet approved developing Karapitiya Teaching Hospital as Sri Lanka’s third national hospital.
Committee appointed to issue permanent land deeds to war heroes under Urumaya.
Government began steps to establish the Sri Lanka Strategic Studies Institute.
Beruwala associations donated Rs. 40,198,902 to the Children of Gaza Fund.
Economic transformation bill creating new institutions was presented to Parliament
India provided solar panels for Sri Lankan Buddhist temples
Government decided to add skills and vocational education to the O-Level curriculum.
Government launched Liyasavi to empower preschool teachers.
Puttalam schools were scheduled to reopen after weather-related closures.
Cabinet approved deed transfers and Treasury-funded exemptions for 50,000 low-income housing owners.
Minister requested Rs. 611.5 million Treasury funding for a trust fund covering 12,230 homes.
Government planned Parliament submission of economic transformation and public finance bills.
Authorities ordered Puttalam schools closed after severe flooding and weather impacts.
Officials advised dengue-control actions and school awareness activities during eradication week.
President will appoint 400 graduate teachers in Jaffna.
Puttalam district schools were ordered closed because of adverse weather.
Development work began on the Gothatuwa wetland park.
The wetland park project received a 180 million rupee allocation.
United States agreed to support training and other needs for Sri Lanka’s oceanographic survey group.
Sri Lanka decided to establish a domestic oceanographic survey committee.
President’s Fund and TRC planned 5,000 ICT scholarships for Advanced Level students.
Cabinet approved restarting Suraksha student insurance nationwide from June.
Government planned modern agricultural facilities across 100 divisional secretariat areas.
Government plans digital transactions programme to prevent corruption in public institutions.
United States plans free English classes for students in Northern Province.
Government plans AI-enabled agricultural modernisation across 100 administrative divisions.
Education Ministry allocation funded Jaffna medical faculty training building construction.
An additional Rs.130 million is estimated to complete the unfinished building.
President is scheduled to open Jaffna medical faculty training building.
Foundation stone was laid for a new lawyers’ office at Kandy court complex.
World Bank-funded Karumpulliyan Kulam water supply project began in Mullaitivu.
Budget allocated Rs. 250 million for Paliyaru water project serving northern districts.
Paliyaru water supply project was inaugurated in Vellankulam, Mannar.
President ordered construction of an Ashraf memorial museum in Kalmunai.
Aswesuma payments reached 966,994 beneficiaries in May, with eligible recipients unpaid.
Two Colombo flood mitigation projects had reported expenditure of Rs. 203 million.
Government reported Rs. 1 million spent on Kalupalama gate-mounted flood pumps.
Rs. 295 million was allocated for Colombo canal maintenance and rehabilitation.
President appointed a committee to accelerate state-land allocation for service personnel.
Presidential Fund and TRC introduced ICT scholarships for Advanced-Level students.
Education ministry proposed 1,220 school clusters and 350 supervisory committees nationwide.
President opened the National Institute of Plantation Management's new building.
Cabinet approved starting Advanced-Level classes immediately after Ordinary-Level examinations.
Cabinet approved amendments to the mechanism granting state residential land to service personnel.
Sri Lanka plans to gazette 20 additional places as sacred sites during 2024.
Matale Kshetraram Rajamaha Viharaya was gazetted as Sri Lanka’s 130th sacred site.
About 3,000 nurses from the 2019/2020 period have been appointed.
A further 3,000 nurses are expected to be appointed.
Beneficiary selection occurred for India-supported plantation housing in Bogawantalawa.
India announced AYUSH scholarships covering tuition, living allowances and accommodation for Sri Lankan students.
India began a two-week governance and skills programme for 40 Sri Lankan civil officials.
Sri Lanka Transport Board permanently appointed 1,000 drivers and conductors.
Parliamentary committee approved a proposal for concessionary vehicle import licences for MPs.
Authorities began filling teacher vacancies across 425 Sabaragamuwa schools.
The President opened Sri Lanka Nursing University.
Sri Lankan Army began an amnesty period for soldiers absent without leave.
The Army temporarily removed 11,985 absent soldiers from their regimental centres.
Private operator announced passenger ferry service from Nagapattinam to Kankesanthurai.
President proposed next year’s allocation for Buddhist teachings and artificial intelligence research.
Government submitted women’s empowerment and gender equality bills to Parliament.
Women’s empowerment bills were submitted to Parliament to establish a national commission.
Provincial veterinary authorities and Trincomalee council conducted stray-dog sterilisation.
Cabinet approved Sri Lanka’s Digital Strategy 2030.
Government arranged smart classrooms for 1,000 schools and plans 500 more.
Sri Lanka allocated Rs. 750 million for the Pinnawala-Kitulgala tourism corridor.
New rural health station opened in Periya Palam, Muthur.
President ordered completion of Bingiriya industrial-zone infrastructure works by year-end.
Appointment letters issued to 2,100 newly recruited Grama Niladhari officers.
Health Ministry is recruiting 3,000 nurses and filling 1,000 existing vacancies.
Litro's new Mabima gas terminal was scheduled to open.
Nativa Capital proposed a $100 million Anuradhapura modern agriculture investment.
Sri Lanka, CVF and Nativa Capital signed an agriculture and forestry cooperation agreement.
Presidential Fund launched new scholarships for pirivena and IT students
Health Ministry began recruiting 3,000 nurses for government hospitals
Cabinet approved Adani wind-power project tariff and electricity purchase tender
Appointments scheduled for 1,942 newly recruited Grama Niladhari officers
Appointments scheduled for 1,942 newly recruited Grama Niladhari officers
Applications invited to fill vacancies for Office on Missing Persons members
Government will again authorise egg imports from India
India-Sri Lanka passenger ferry service scheduled to resume on May 13.
